title: Paris vs London: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Paris and London based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

categories.title: 🥐 Food & Dining
categories.summary: This is genuinely one of the most debated categories among European travelers, and it used to be a no-brainer: Paris. categories.title: 🎒 Day Trips
categories.summary: Both cities are excellent bases for day trips, with radically different options. Paris unlocks some of the world's greatest palaces and gardens within an hour; London opens up England's most beloved historic towns.

faqs.question: Is Paris or London better for first-time visitors to Europe?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent first stops in Europe, but they offer very different experiences. Paris is the world's most visited city for good reason — the Louvre, Eiffel Tower, and Versailles are in a league of their own, and the city is supremely walkable. faqs.question: How far apart are Paris and London?
faqs.answer: Paris and London are approximately 340 km (213 miles) apart. The Eurostar train takes 2 hours 15 minutes from London St Pancras to Paris Gare du Nord and costs £39–£200+ depending on booking time. faqs.question: Is Paris more expensive than London?
faqs.answer: It depends on the category. London is generally more expensive overall — accommodation costs around 20-30% more, and eating out at restaurants is pricier. faqs.question: Which city has better food — Paris or London?
faqs.answer: Paris wins for French cuisine — croissants, brasseries, bistros, and haute cuisine are unmatched anywhere on Earth. faqs.question: How many days do you need in Paris vs London?
faqs.answer: For a first visit: minimum 3 full days in each city, ideally 4–5. Paris's main highlights (Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Notre-Dame, Versailles, Montmartre, Marais) can be covered in 4 days, but you'll want more time to wander properly. faqs.question: Is it worth visiting both Paris and London on one trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. The Eurostar makes it one of the easiest two-city combos in Europe. Most travelers do London + Paris in 7–10 days. faqs.answer: Paris wins on metro coverage and cost. The Paris Métro has 16 lines covering the entire city, with flat fare tickets at €2.15 per ride or a day pass (t+ carnet) for much less.
